title: Formulas for Everyday Analysis
description: CAT 100 textbook section connecting formulas for everyday analysis to a spreadsheet formula trace with locked-constant labels and a bottom-row verification note, reader notes, support moments, and revision evidence.

learning_objectives.statement: Predict how a relative, absolute ($F$1), or mixed (B$1, $A2) reference rewrites when a formula is copied down or across
Choose relative references for per-row inputs and absolute references for shared constants, and justify the lock pattern in a trace
Verify a copied formula column by reading the formula in the last filled cell, not just the first
Explain SUM, AVERAGE, and COUNT semantics, including why AVERAGE skips blanks but counts a stray zero

alignment_method: deterministic lexical mapping v2 with direct-evidence fallback; instructor review required
